requirements.requirement: The system must invoke the credential completeness scoring logic from EVAL-CRED-002 within evaluate_care_facade when assembling provider evaluation responses.
The system must include a credential_completeness_score field in the provider evaluation response payload.
The system must include a credential_completeness_breakdown object containing degrees, licenses, and taxonomy completeness components in the response.
The system must ensure the credential_completeness_score is normalized to the schema defined in EVAL-CRED-001 (0-1 or 0-100) before returning the response.
The system must preserve existing provider evaluation response fields without modification when adding credential completeness data.
The system must return credential completeness data for every provider where NPI data is successfully retrieved.
The system must return a credential_completeness_score of 0 and an empty breakdown when all credential-related fields are missing from NPI data.
The system must handle partial NPI data by computing and returning a partial credential_completeness_score based on available fields.
The system must not throw an unhandled exception if credential scoring logic fails, and must instead omit the credential fields from the response.
The system must log an error event when credential scoring logic fails during facade execution.
The system must structure credential completeness fields in a way that is directly consumable by downstream explanation or UX layers without additional transformation.
The system must ensure that credential completeness data is included consistently across all provider evaluation responses generated by evaluate_care_facade.
The system must enable downstream LLM components to access credential_completeness_score and breakdown fields in the response payload without additional API calls.
The system must present credential completeness data in a semantically labeled structure that supports LLM explanation generation (e.g., clearly named fields for degrees, licenses, taxonomy).
